title: Runtime tree accounts for all wall time
body:
The -s runtime tree has two branches, seeding and alignment, and neither the top level nor the seeding branch sums to its wall. Query indexing, target indexing and build_pipeline are untimed or printed and discarded. The mmseqs db writes and the prog-mode bookkeeping fall into seeding's [misc.]. The alignment leaves print thread-second sums that read as a bug beside the branch wall.

Done when every branch's leaves plus [misc.] sum to the branch wall, runtime equals the sum of its branches, and the alignment leaves show derived wall time.

Format, settled 2026-09-28: the tree stays. Extra data points go in square brackets. Only the alignment branch gets a column header, with a dashed rule, carried on the tree rail. No new output file, no event log, no timestamps. The target tree is in the notes.

Behavior does not change apart from build_pipeline moving ahead of seed(). The progress println!s in search.rs stay as user feedback.

Open: --stats-results-path (args.rs:421) is validated at args.rs:161 and never written. Either wire it to write the same tree to a file or remove it.

notes.author: Jack Roddy/415c993d
notes.text:
Target tree, numbers illustrative. Serial branches keep today's shape; only alignment gets the header and rule.

runtime: 557.31s
 └─ setup:       9.20s ( 1.65%)
     ├─ query index          1.02s
     ├─ target index         2.10s
     ├─ pipeline build       5.93s
     └─ [misc.]              0.15s
 └─ seeding:   347.02s (62.27%)
     ├─ db write             4.11s
     ├─ prefilter          289.40s
     ├─ align               36.04s   [4 iterations]
     │   ├─ 1                3.10s
     │   ├─ 2                6.22s
     │   ├─ 3               12.40s
     │   └─ 4               14.32s
     ├─ convertalis          2.80s
     ├─ seed index           1.20s
     └─ [misc.]              1.47s
 └─ alignment: 201.34s (36.13%)   [48 threads, cpu 9,610s, 99.4% busy]
     │                        wall        %      cpu
     │                     -------   ------   ------
     ├─ cloud search       113.02s   56.13%   5,425s
     ├─ backward            34.20s   16.99%   1,642s
     ├─ forward             29.10s   14.45%   1,397s
     ├─ posterior            9.31s    4.62%     447s
     ├─ optimal accuracy     8.02s    3.98%     385s
     └─ [misc.]              7.69s    3.82%     369s
 └─ [misc.]      0.75s ( 0.13%)

Why share × wall and no idle row: there is no measurable per-stage wall in a parallel run, so leaf wall is a definition. share × wall spreads any idle pro rata over the leaves; cpu ÷ threads would show idle as its own row. At full utilization they are equal, and the busy figure on the branch line already says how much idle there is. Decided 2026-09-28.

Origin: a handoff from nail-benchmarks (benchmarks/stage-times) written 2026-09-28 against 837ba60. Its mechanism (a phase event log written via --stats-results-path, with timestamps) was rejected; the gaps it found are what this milestone closes.
